haiku-low.q1: The API checks the unfiltered reports.row_count. At 10,000 rows or fewer, it returns the CSV directly in the response and the page saves it. Above 10,000, it queues a background job, returns 202, and the user later gets an emailed 24-hour link.
haiku-low.q2: The insert violates the partial unique index, so the API returns 200 with the existing queued or running export's id and status, and queues nothing new.
haiku-low.q3: The emailed signed link expires after 24 hours. The stored file is removed by the bucket's lifecycle rule 7 days after creation. Incomplete uploads are aborted or discarded by the bucket after 24 hours.
haiku-low.q4: Up to three attempts, with retries waiting 60 s then 300 s. After the last failure, the row is set to failed with error and finished_at, a failure email is sent, and the page shows the failed label.
haiku-low.q5: Both the small and large export paths read report rows from the read replica. The export record itself lives in the primary database.
haiku-low.q6: Status is stored in the report_exports row in the primary database. The page keeps no state: on load it calls the latest-export endpoint, and while queued or running it polls every 5 seconds.
haiku-low.q7: It reads 5,000 rows at a time from the replica, encodes them as CSV into an 8 MB buffer, and uploads each full buffer as a multipart part. Memory holds only one batch plus one buffer, and the upload is completed at the end.
haiku-low.q8: Written data stays in an uncompleted, invisible multipart upload. On exception it is aborted; on crash or timeout the bucket discards it within 24 hours. The next attempt starts a new upload from the first row; nothing carries over.
haiku-low.q9: They are stored on the report_exports row at insert time. The job payload carries only export_id, and the job loads filters and columns from that row in the primary database.
haiku-low.q10: The partial unique index on (user_id, report_id) where status is queued or running. A conflicting insert is rejected, and the API returns the existing active export.
haiku-low.q11: The file must be completed and object_key saved, and a 24-hour signed URL created. If the job runs again after succeeded or failed, it does nothing; if running with object_key set, it only sends the email.
haiku-low.q12: If the replica fails before any bytes are sent, the API returns 503. If it fails mid-stream, the connection is dropped. Either way the page saves no file and shows the failure message. Nothing retries automatically.

sonnet.q1: The unfiltered reports.row_count decides. 10,000 or fewer: CSV returned directly in the response (200, text/csv), no job or storage. More than 10,000: API saves an export record, queues a background job, returns 202 at once; the job writes the file to the exports bucket and emails the user a link valid 24 hours.
sonnet.q2: The partial unique index on (user_id, report_id) where status is queued/running makes the insert fail. The API then returns 200 with the existing active export's id and status, and queues nothing new.
sonnet.q3: The link works for 24 hours (signed URL, 86400 s). The file is removed by the bucket's lifecycle rule 7 days after creation; no cleanup job is needed.
sonnet.q4: Up to 3 attempts (retries after 60 s, then 300 s). After attempt 3 fails, on_final_failure sets the row to failed (error, finished_at), the page shows 'Export failed. Click Download CSV to try again.', and the user is emailed a 'report_export_failed' message (if that email fails, it is just logged). The user can click again to start a new export.
sonnet.q5: The read replica (both small and large paths).
sonnet.q6: In the report_exports row (status column) in the primary database. The page polls GET /api/exports/{export_id} every 5 seconds while queued/running. On reopening, it calls GET /api/reports/{report_id}/exports/latest to get the user's newest export, then polls if still active. The page holds no state of its own.
sonnet.q7: Via multipart upload in streaming fashion: read 5,000-row batches from the replica by row_id, encode to CSV in an in-memory buffer, upload a part each time the buffer reaches 8 MB, then upload the remainder, complete_multipart and save object_key. Memory holds only one batch plus one 8 MB buffer (about 115 parts for ~900 MB). The document does not mention the 512 MB worker figure itself.
sonnet.q8: On an exception the job calls abort_multipart and re-raises. If the worker crashes or times out (30 min), the upload is never completed, nothing becomes visible, and the bucket discards it after 24 h. Nothing carries over: the next attempt starts again at step 6 with a new upload from the first row. (If complete_multipart succeeded but saving object_key failed, the next attempt rewrites the file and complete_multipart replaces it.)
sonnet.q9: They are stored (frozen) in the filters and columns fields of the report_exports row in the primary database, taken from the request. The job payload carries only export_id; the job loads the row and uses its stored filters and columns.
sonnet.q10: The partial unique index on (user_id, report_id) where status in ('queued','running') in the report_exports table, created by the migration. The second insert violates it.
sonnet.q11: The file must be complete: complete_multipart done and object_key saved on the row. If the job runs again: if the row is succeeded or failed, it returns and does nothing; if running with object_key set, it skips writing and goes straight to step 8 (signed URL, email, mark succeeded). Otherwise it sets running and rewrites the file.
sonnet.q12: If the replica fails before any bytes are sent, the API returns 503; if mid-stream, the API drops the connection. Either way the page saves no file and shows 'Export failed. Click Download CSV to try again.' Nothing retries automatically.
